gen-gf-gabarito-gf-poly: Gabarito draws everything as if with a single nib, its open terminals letting the counters flow outward. And Poly, a classic serif, brings the bookish side, with bowls that thin slightly at the sides and hairlines you can actually see.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-quattrocento: Loose, expressive, drawn in one stroke. Gabarito keeps every line at a single weight with no contrast, while Quattrocento, a text serif, lets its horizontals run a touch slimmer than its verticals and leaves daylight inside each curve.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-radley: Dignified, first of all, in Radley's case. Gabarito has no swelling where curves meet stems, so the pair's real strength is how that smooth heading sits against a serif with sturdy downstrokes and slender turns.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-roboto-serif: Roboto Serif reads with big open eyes and letters set well apart, a mild thick-thin rhythm running through it. Gabarito does expressive best, with no modulation at all, and Roboto Serif, a classic serif, handles the moderate swing between heavy and light.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sahitya: Sahitya reads like a text serif, its thin strokes only slightly lighter than the thick ones and its s and c left uncrowded. And a longer passage would feel steady and bookish, like a round brush barely pressed, against Gabarito's heading curves that never thin at the shoulders.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Gabarito's most distinctive trait is its open-cut terminals, which let counters flow outward from strokes that never change width. Sawarabi Mincho, a serif, would carry a long passage with moderate thick-thin transitions and terminals cut well short of the bowl.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sedan: Sedan is a text serif with a mellow range of stroke weights and terminals held far from the stroke body. But shrink Gabarito to small sizes and its lack of any thin hairline leaves less to distinguish it from that steady body.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-sedan-sc: One nib, no shading, plenty of personality. Gabarito is at its best with plain, unshaded lines, and Sedan SC, a text serif, is at its best with broad open counters and a middle-of-the-road contrast.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-shippori-mincho: Shippori Mincho reads as a text serif with modest contrast, noticeable only on close look, and generous openings in every curve. Gabarito's lines keep their width through every turn, so the two sit together as a smooth heading over sturdy thin and slightly heavier thick strokes.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-shippori-mincho-b1: Shippori Mincho B1 is a refined, editorial classic serif with a c opened wide like a crescent wrench and hairlines of reasonable sturdiness. Yet Gabarito, with no brush-style pressure swell anywhere, gives the pair its strongest quality: a smooth expressive heading against medium contrast.
